To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spectroscopic strengths for weakly-bound proton states are reduced relative to shell-model predictions, while the spectroscopic strengths of strongly-bound neutron states are enhanced.

the spectroscopic factors extracted from one-proton knockout of weakly bound valance protons are significantly reduced from shell-model predictions, while the spectroscopic factors for one-neutron knockout of strongly bound neutrons are not significantly reduced from shell model predictions.

the spectroscopic strengths for the weakly-bound proton single-particle states and the strongly-bound neutron single-particle states in the 9 Be(28S,27P)X and 28S(9Be,27S)X reactions are reduced by factors of 0.80 and 0.40 respectively, relative to shell model predictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spectroscopic properties of nuclei far from stability.
the study of the nuclear structure of exotic nuclei using one-nucleus knockout reactions.
the study of the structure of nuclei at the extremes of binding and the study of the effects of binding energy on nucleon spectroscopic factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spectroscopic strengths for the more weakly-bound nucleons are reduced by about 20% and those for the more strongly-bound nucleons are increased by about 20%.
the nucleon spectroscopy is strongly reduced at the weakly bound Fermi surface, and is reduced at the more-bound surface.
the spectroscopic strength of the more-bound species is less than that of the more weak species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nucleons in the weakly bound proton systems are less strongly correlated than those in the weakly-bound neutron systems and that the nucleons of both the excess and deficient species at the strongly-bound Fermi surface of the neutron-deficient systems are more strongly correlated.
the spectroscopic strength of a nucleon is reduced in a nuclear system by a factor of order 0:8 when the nucleon is weakly bound, and of order 0-4 when the nucleon has a strong binding energy.
in asymmetric nuclear matter the nucleon spectroscopy is modified by the presence of the nuclear mean field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spectroscopic strengths are reduced in the removal of nucleons from the weakly bound Fermi surfaces and that this reduction is more pronounced for the removal of protons than for neutrons.
the spectroscopic strength is reduced by a factor of 0.8 to 0.9 for weakly bound nucleons, and by a factor of about 0.4 to 0.5 for strongly bound nucleons.
the reduction in spectroscopic strength of the more bound nucleons in asymmetric systems is larger for one-proton knockout than for one-neutron knockout.
